# PostgreSQL invalid indexes from failed CONCURRENTLY builds

# PostgreSQL invalid indexes from failed CONCURRENTLY builds — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for PostgreSQL invalid indexes from failed CONCURRENTLY builds. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-30 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## Definitions

- [statement] Inspect pg_index.indisvalid for query eligibility and indisready for INSERT/UPDATE maintenance; indisready=false means writes ignore the index, so invalid does not imply one universal maintenance state. (low confidence) — https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/catalog-pg-index.html

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Deadlocks or uniqueness errors during concurrent scanning can leave invalid indexes that queries cannot use; pganalyze independently documents failed or aborted concurrent builds as a typical cause. (high confidence) — https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-createindex.html · keywords: PostgreSQL invalid indexes from failed CONCURRENTLY builds · also: https://www.dbi-services.com/blog/create-index-concurrently-in-postgresql/, https://pganalyze.com/docs/checks/schema/index_invalid
- [statement] A unique concurrent build starts enforcing uniqueness during its second scan; failure there can leave uniqueness enforcement active even though queries cannot use the index. (medium confidence) — https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-createindex.html · keywords: PostgreSQL invalid indexes from failed CONCURRENTLY builds · also: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/catalog-pg-index.html
- [statement] Blind retries can fail with relation already exists; IF NOT EXISTS only checks name existence and cannot establish that the existing index is usable or matches the intended definition. (medium confidence) — https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-createindex.html · keywords: PostgreSQL invalid indexes from failed CONCURRENTLY builds · also: https://www.dbi-services.com/blog/create-index-concurrently-in-postgresql/
- [statement] A running concurrent build is initially invalid too; indisvalid=false alone cannot establish that creation has failed. (medium confidence) — https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-createindex.html · keywords: PostgreSQL invalid indexes from failed CONCURRENTLY builds · also: https://github-wiki-see.page/m/FullmetalBober/Indexterity/wiki/Architecture

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Concurrent creation uses multiple transactions; cancellation after catalog creation can leave an INVALID index, unlike an aborted ordinary build. (medium confidence) — https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-createindex.html · keywords: PostgreSQL invalid indexes from failed CONCURRENTLY builds · also: https://www.dbi-services.com/blog/create-index-concurrently-in-postgresql/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Invalid artifacts can occupy disk and incur write maintenance despite providing no query acceleration; dbi demonstrates a sequential scan and subsequent index growth. (high confidence) — https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-createindex.html · keywords: PostgreSQL invalid indexes from failed CONCURRENTLY builds · also: https://www.dbi-services.com/blog/create-index-concurrently-in-postgresql/, https://pganalyze.com/docs/checks/schema/index_invalid
- [statement] Drop and recreate a failed index, or use REINDEX INDEX CONCURRENTLY; the latter is the REINDEX form that can concurrently rebuild an invalid index. (medium confidence) — https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-createindex.html · keywords: PostgreSQL invalid indexes from failed CONCURRENTLY builds · also: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-reindex.html
- [statement] After failed concurrent reindexing, an INVALID _ccnew artifact represents the unfinished replacement; drop it and retry. An INVALID _ccold artifact is the old index left after successful rebuilding; drop it. Numeric suffixes may follow these names. (low confidence) — https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-reindex.html
